content:
Negative exponents make Class 8 students nervous — until someone says the quiet part aloud: a MINUS in the exponent just means "flip the fraction". After that, this becomes the fastest chapter on the paper. Below sits a free IMO Class 8 Exponents and Powers online test — 10 Olympiad-pattern MCQs with instant scoring and a worked explanation under every answer. Eight out of ten is the score to beat.

What the IMO asks from Exponents and Powers in Class 8

  • Negative exponents and reciprocals.
  • All five exponent laws, now with negative powers.
  • Standard form for very small numbers.
  • Comparing and simplifying power expressions.
  • Solving for x in equations like 5ˣ ÷ 5⁻³ = 5⁵.

Key facts and formulas to revise first

  • a⁻ⁿ = 1/aⁿ: a negative exponent flips, it never makes the value negative.
  • (2/3)⁻² = (3/2)² = 9/4 — flip first, then square.
  • 0.000035 in standard form is 3.5 × 10⁻⁵ — count the hops to just past the first non-zero digit.
  • Laws work for negatives too: 5ˣ ÷ 5⁻³ = 5ˣ⁺³.

Mistakes that cost Olympiad marks

  • Reading 2⁻³ as −8 (it is 1/8).
  • Moving the decimal point the wrong way for small-number standard form.
  • Adding exponents when the bases are different.

questions.explanation: Using the power-of-a-power rule: (2⁴)³ = 2¹² and (2³)² = 2⁶. So the expression becomes 2¹² × 2⁶ ÷ 2¹⁵ = 2¹²⁺⁶⁻¹⁵ = 2³ = 8.
Using (aˣ)^(y) = a^(xy): first term = a^((m-n)(m+n)) = a^(m2)-n². Second = a^(n2)-p². Third = a^(p2)-m². Product = a^(m2)-n²+n²-p²+p²-m² = a⁰ = 1.
3.2 × 10⁶ = 3200000 and 8.1 × 10⁵ = 810000. Since 3200000 > 810000, 3.2 × 10⁶ is larger. When exponents differ, the number with the higher power of 10 is usually larger.

questions.q: How many times is 4 × 10⁷ larger than 8 × 10⁴?
If (3.6 × 10⁵) × (a × 10^(b)) = 1.8 × 10⁹, and a is a single-digit integer, find a × b.
